nodes.description: OER performance with potential-dependent and time-dependent resistance measurement via EIS

cause_of_resistance_increase.value: possible structural changes and gas bubble formation

nodes.source_text: we measured the R_HFR,M of an anodically treated Co planar electrode (i.e., Co(OH)2-coated Co electrode) at different potentials during OER. The resistance value is potential-dependent, and those at reaction potentials are lower than that at OCP (except the one before OER, time = 0 s). Moreover, as the OER continues, the R_u increases, indicating possible structural changes. At 1.0 V where bubbles are generated rapidly on the electrode, the R_u is higher than at other potentials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is used to measure high-frequency resistance (R_HFR) by fitting the high-frequency region with an equivalent circuit, typically the Randles circuit, to determine uncompensated resistance (R_u) for iR compensation in electrocatalytic studies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resistance is obtained by fitting the high-frequency region (HFR) of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data with an equivalent circuit (often the Randles circuit), denoted as R_HFR.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curves at typical scan rates of 1-10 mV/s are used to evaluate electrocatalytic performance; however, non-Faradaic currents from electrical double layer evolution complicate iR compensation, particularly for nanomaterial-coated electrodes with large electrochemical surface areas (ECSAs).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For most polarization tests in the literature, LSV is used, and the potential scan rate is between 1 and 10 mV s−1. In these cases, the non-Faradaic current is inevitable, especially for nanomaterial-coated electrodes with large electrochemical surface areas (ECSAs).

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope analysis is highly sensitive to iR compensation; polycrystalline Pt in 0.05 M H2SO4 exhibits Tafel slope decrease from 31 to 23 mV/dec when iR compensation factor increases from 90% to 95%, demonstrating that iR compensation significantly affects mechanistic interpretation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Chen et al. demonstrated that the Tafel slope of polycrystalline Pt in 0.05 M H2SO4 decreases from 31 to 23 mV dec−1 when the factor rises from 90% to 95%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Polarization curves of lab-developed HER catalyst MoNi4 and OER catalyst NiFe LDH demonstrate that 100% iR compensation reduces overpotential by 60-70 mV at 100 mA/cm² and 500-600 mV at 1 A/cm², sufficient to change catalyst performance rating from mediocre to promising.
nodes.evidence_snippet: at 100 mA cm−2, 100% iR compensation reduces the overpotential of lab-developed HER and OER catalysts by 60-70 mV. It becomes even more dramatic at higher currents (1 A cm−2), reaching 500-600 mV, enough to change the rating of the catalyst from "mediocre" to "promising".

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements of anodically treated Co(OH)2-coated Co electrode show potential-dependent R_HFR values during oxygen evolution reaction, with resistance at reaction potentials lower than at open-circuit potential and increasing over time, indicating structural changes and gas bubble formation effects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We measured the R_HFR,M of an anodically treated Co planar electrode (i.e., Co(OH)2-coated Co electrode) at different potentials during OER. The resistance value is potential-dependent, and those at reaction potentials are lower than that at OCP (except the one before OER, time = 0 s). Moreover, as the OER continues, the R_u increases, indicating possible structural changes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry curves of anodically treated Co(OH)2-coated Co electrode for oxygen evolution reaction comparing on-the-fly and after-the-scan iR compensation methods demonstrate that after-the-scan method with predetermined R_u results in overcorrection when gas bubbles dynamically alter solution resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: LSV curves of anodically treated Co planar electrode for OER, comparing on-the-fly and after-the-scan (PF) correction methods (R_u = 10.5 ohm is used/input)... after-the-scan method results in overcorrection.

nodes.characterization_summary: Kelvin four-terminal sensing is identified as a preferred method to measure contact resistance (R_contact) and catalyst material resistance (R_catalyst) separately in modified electrodes, though no experimental data from the present work are provided.
nodes.evidence_snippet: R_contact and R_catalyst can be measured in many ways, and two preferred methods are Kelvin four-terminal sensing and measurement via an interdigitated array electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Scanning electrochemical microscopy is cited as a technique that demonstrates potential distribution on modified electrode surfaces is not homogeneous, with local electric field and R_catalyst at individual active sites depending on morphology and structure, though no original data are presented.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For such electrodes, it is well-known that the potential distribution on the surface is not homogeneous. The local electric field and R_catalyst at the individual active sites depend on the morphology and structure, as many scanning electrochemical microscopy studies demonstrated.

nodes.characterization_summary: Staircase linear sweep voltammetry (S-LSV) is recommended as an alternative to conventional LSV for polarization tests in electrocatalysis, where potential changes in large steps and non-Faradaic current decreases rapidly, allowing more precise iR compensation with Faradaic current dominance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, instead of LSV, we suggest researchers use another electrochemical technique, staircase linear sweep voltammetry (S-LSV), to do the polarization tests. In short, the potential changes in large steps, and the non-Faradaic current decreases rapidly within a few seconds when reaching a new step.
